name: Bootloader Size Check
blurb: whether application and bootloader regions fit
intro: Lays the bootloader, one or two application slots, an optional swap scratch sector and a reserved data area onto the chip's real erase sectors (each region must start and end on a sector boundary so it can be erased alone), then checks that each image fits with your growth margin and that the application's vector table is aligned for VTOR.

inputs.label: Page / sector size
inputs.help: STM32G4/L4: 2K, STM32F1 HD: 2K, nRF52: 4K, RP2040: 4K, SAMD21: 256 bytes (row).

inputs.label: Sector list
inputs.help: In address order; n*size repeats. STM32F407 1 MB: 16K*4, 64K, 128K*7.

inputs.label: Bootloader image size
inputs.help: text + data from arm-none-eabi-size, or the .bin size.

inputs.label: Bootloader reserve
inputs.help: Blank: the image size rounded up to whole sectors, plus the margin.

inputs.label: Image header + trailer
inputs.help: Bytes per slot the bootloader keeps; MCUboot: 0x200 header plus a trailer of a few hundred bytes.

inputs.label: Reserved data at the end
inputs.help: Settings or EEPROM emulation; rounded up to whole sectors. 0 for none.

examples.title: STM32G4 512 KB, A/B update, 2 KB pages

usage: Give the flash start and size, the erase sector layout (uniform with page size, or list like '16K*4, 64K, 128K*7'), bootloader and application image sizes in bytes (K = 1024 or hex accepted), the number of slots (1, 2 or 2s for MCUboot swap-scratch), per-slot header/trailer bytes, a reserved data area at the end, the vector table entry count and a growth margin in %. It returns the region table with addresses, fit and headroom per image, the VTOR alignment check and linker MEMORY lines. Use it when planning a bootloader partition or when an image outgrows its slot.
sources: Armv7-M Architecture Reference Manual B3.2.5 (VTOR: table aligned to the entry count rounded up to a power of two, minimum 128 bytes)
MCUboot design documentation (image slots, swap using scratch: scratch at least the largest sector)
Device reference manuals for sector layouts (e.g. ST RM0090 table 5 for STM32F4)
